title: Funds management: Constitutions
subject: This guide addresses the requirements under the Corporations Act 2001 for the constitutions of registered managed investment schemes, corporate collective investment vehicles (CCIVs), and Australian passport funds. It provides guidance on the content and amendment of constitutions, including matters such as consideration and issue price, rights of members, and compliance obligations.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Act 2001 to assist responsible entities, corporate directors, and Australian passport fund operators in meeting their legal obligations regarding fund constitutions. It explains ASIC's interpretation of the relevant legislative provisions and its approach to exercising powers such as granting relief. The guide is intended for those involved in the establishment, operation, and governance of retail investment funds.
ruling: ASIC states that a constitution for a registered scheme must meet the requirements in s 601GA of the Corporations Act, including provisions for the consideration to acquire an interest and the rights of members. For retail funds, ASIC expects that the constitution clearly sets out the basis for calculating consideration and issue prices to ensure fairness and transparency. ASIC provides guidance on when it may grant relief from these requirements, such as through legislative instruments. ASIC also interprets the law to require that any amendments to the constitution comply with member approval and notification provisions, and that class rights are adequately protected. The guide outlines ASIC's regulatory approach to assessing compliance and the circumstances in which it will take enforcement action.
